vendors.name: dbt Semantic Layer (MetricFlow)
vendors.tagline: Metric definitions in dbt projects, compiled to SQL by the open-source MetricFlow engine.
vendors.verdictNote: MetricFlow gives governed metrics that agents query through the dbt MCP server, but the Semantic Layer APIs need a dbt Starter or higher plan.

artifacts.name: dbt Semantic Layer (semantic models and metrics in YAML)
dbt MCP server OAuth for AI tools (labeled Beta)
Apache Ossie semantic layer documents (dbt v1.12 and later)

metrics.n: Metrics are defined in YAML (simple, ratio, derived, cumulative, conversion). MetricFlow compiles them to SQL for each warehouse.

dimensions.n: Categorical and time dimensions are declared on model columns, with time granularity. MetricFlow adds joins at query time.

relationships.n: Entities (primary, foreign, unique, natural) mark join keys. MetricFlow builds joins across semantic models from them.

synonyms.n: Description and label fields on semantic models, dimensions, and metrics. No synonyms field in the docs.

verifiedQueries.n: No question-to-SQL store. Saved queries (GA) group metrics, dimensions, and filters, and the MCP list_saved_queries tool returns them.

nl2sql.n: MCP text_to_sql tool generates SQL from project context. It uses dbt Copilot actions and is off when AI is disabled.

ontology.n: No separate ontology layer. Teams model entities, dimensions, and metrics in semantic models.

graph.n: No graph query language. Semantic models form a join graph that MetricFlow uses internally.

vector.n: The MCP get_related_models tool finds similar models with semantic search. The broader search tool is labeled Alpha.

mcp.n: MCP server exposes Semantic Layer, Discovery, SQL, and Admin API tools. Remote server is on all plans; tools vary.

governance.n: Queries run under a warehouse credential, so platform access policies apply. Discovery API and MCP expose lineage. Plan limits apply.

openStandard.n: MetricFlow is Apache 2.0. dbt v1.12 and later also read Apache Ossie JSON documents as semantic models.

offers: Metrics, entities, and dimensions defined once in YAML and compiled to SQL by MetricFlow, so agents do not write joins.
MCP server tools list metrics, get dimensions, query metrics, and run text_to_sql.
Saved queries group common metric and dimension combinations and are listed over MCP.
MetricFlow is Apache 2.0, and dbt v1.12 reads Apache Ossie documents.
Works with Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, Postgres, and Trino.
gaps: Answers only modeled questions. In dbt's April 2026 benchmark, questions needing too many entity hops got no answer.
Semantic Layer APIs and integrations need a dbt Starter, Enterprise, or Enterprise+ plan.
No synonyms field. Only description and label carry business wording.
No stored question-to-SQL pairs and no ontology layer.
fillWith: Text-to-SQL for questions outside the model
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model your core metrics and dimensions in dbt, then connect an agent through the dbt MCP server. Let the agent query metrics for modeled questions. Fall back to text-to-SQL only for questions outside the model.

snippet.title: Semantic model on a dbt model (dbt v1.12 and later)
snippet.code:
models:
  - name: fact_transactions
    semantic_model:
      enabled: true
    agg_time_dimension: transaction_date
    columns:
      - name: transaction_date
        granularity: day
        dimension:
          type: time
    metrics:
      - name: transaction_total
        type: simple
        agg: sum
        expr: transaction_total

vendors.name: Cube (Core and Cloud)
vendors.tagline: Semantic layer with cubes and views, plus Cloud agents, Analytics Chat, and MCP.
vendors.verdictNote: Cubes, views, access policies, AI context, certified queries, a Chat API, a hosted MCP server, and Ossie conversion (Preview) are documented.

artifacts.name: Chat API for Cube agents (Premium and Enterprise plans)
AI context and certified queries (code-first agent config)

metrics.n: Measures are declared in cubes (count, sum, filtered measures). Views expose them to consumers.

dimensions.n: Dimensions, hierarchies, and time dimensions are declared in cubes and included in views.

relationships.n: Joins between cubes declare relationship (such as many_to_one). Views use join_path to pick the route.

synonyms.n: Descriptions are read by the agent. ai_context in meta on views and members is agent-only, up to 2,000 characters.

verifiedQueries.n: Certified queries are Markdown files with a user_request and SQL. The agent uses them as trusted examples.

nl2sql.n: Analytics Chat and the Chat API answer questions over the semantic layer. Chat API needs a Premium or Enterprise plan.

ontology.n: No ontology layer found in the docs. Cubes and views are the modeling objects.

graph.n: No graph query language found in the docs.

vector.n: No vector or semantic search feature found in the docs index.

mcp.n: Hosted MCP server with OAuth, available on all plans. The earlier local npm server is deprecated.

governance.n: Access policies combine member access, row filters, and masking by group. Analytics Chat honors the active security context.

openStandard.n: Apache Ossie export and import through the Cube CLI and Platform API. Docs label it Preview; contact support to enable.

offers: Cubes and views give agents a curated, joined model with measures and dimensions defined once.
Hosted MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor query governed data over OAuth.
Agent configuration lives in the repo: rules, certified queries, and accessible views.
Descriptions and agent-only ai_context in meta guide the agent.
Access policies with row filters and masking apply to agent queries.
gaps: Cube reads only SQL-queryable sources, not files or REST APIs directly.
Chat API needs a Premium or Enterprise plan.
Configuring the agent in the UI is deprecated in favor of code-first setup.
Ossie conversion and Evals are Preview, and Ossie conversion is activated by Cube support.
No ontology, graph, or vector feature found.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model cubes and views on your warehouse, then expose a small set of views to an agent. Use the hosted MCP server or the Chat API. Add rules, ai_context, and certified queries under the agents directory.

snippet.title: A cube with a join, a measure, and a dimension
snippet.code:
cubes:
  - name: users
    sql_table: users

    joins:
      - name: organizations
        relationship: many_to_one
        sql: "{CUBE.organization_id} = {organizations.id}"

    measures:
      - name: count
        type: count
        sql: id

    dimensions:
      - name: country
        sql: country
        type: string

vendors.name: AtScale
vendors.tagline: Enterprise semantic layer with an open modeling language (SML) and an MCP server.
vendors.verdictNote: AtScale models governed metrics in SML, an open YAML format, and serves them to agents through an MCP server.

artifacts.name: Semantic models in Semantic Modeling Language (SML), Apache open source
Natural Language Query (NLQ), announced as private preview
AtScale for Snowflake Semantic Views (XMLA endpoint, private preview coming soon)

metrics.n: Metric and calculation objects in SML define aggregated and derived values, including semi-additive and non-additive metrics.

dimensions.n: Dimension objects declare attributes and hierarchies for drill-down. SML also covers time-based levels.

relationships.n: Model files declare relationships between fact datasets and dimensions, including role-playing relationships.

synonyms.n: Models, dimensions, and metrics have description and label fields. MCP column tools return descriptions. No synonyms field found.

verifiedQueries.n: No stored question-to-SQL examples in the SML reference or MCP tools. The MCP get_sml_skills tool serves query guidance.

nl2sql.n: External agents write SQL through MCP run_query. A first-party NLQ feature was announced as private preview in Sept 2024.

ontology.n: No ontology layer in the SML object list. Objects are models, dimensions, metrics, calculations, and datasets.

graph.n: No graph query language found in the SML reference or MCP tools.

vector.n: No vector search found in the MCP tools or SML reference.

mcp.n: MCP server tools: list_models, explore_columns, focus_columns, run_query, get_outbound_queries. Enabled through Helm values.

governance.n: Row security objects restrict rows by user or group. MCP outbound query audit needs the queries_view role.

openStandard.n: SML is Apache open source with converters and a CLI. AtScale joined the Open Semantic Interchange on 27 Jan 2026.

offers: Metrics, dimensions with hierarchies, and relationships modeled in SML, a YAML format kept in Git.
MCP run_query checks agent SQL against the model before it reaches the warehouse.
MCP column tools return descriptions and sampled values for each column.
Row security objects restrict data by user or group.
MCP server listed in the Databricks MCP Marketplace since Dec 2025.
gaps: No stored question-to-SQL examples and no synonyms field found in the docs.
First-party NLQ was announced as a private preview in Sept 2024. Current docs describe MCP access for external agents.
MCP queries must be SELECT only, one model per query, with no CTEs or subqueries.
Current docs list six warehouses. The Snowflake Semantic Views endpoint is announced, not shipped.
Only SML is open source. The engine is a commercial product.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model metrics in AtScale and enable the MCP server in your Helm values. Point your agent at list_models, explore_columns, and run_query so it stays on governed metrics instead of raw tables.

snippet.title: An SML metric object
snippet.code:
unique_name: m_catalog_sales_coupon_amount_avg
object_type: metric
label: Catalog Sales Average Coupon Amount
calculation_method: average
dataset: catalog_sales
column: cs_sales_price

vendors.name: Wren AI / Wren Engine
vendors.tagline: Open-core GenBI engine and context layer with a modeling definition language (MDL).
vendors.verdictNote: Wren is an open-source semantic engine with MDL models, relationships, cubes, NL-to-SQL pairs, an MCP server, and Apache Ossie import and export.

artifacts.name: Modeling Definition Language (MDL) project: models, relationships, views, cubes
Knowledge base: rules and NL-to-SQL pairs with memory index

metrics.n: Cubes declare measures as expression plus type on a base model or view. Queried with wren cube query.

dimensions.n: Cubes declare dimensions, time dimensions with query-time granularity, and hierarchies. Models declare typed columns.

relationships.n: relationships.yml declares join type (such as MANY_TO_ONE) and an equality condition between two models.

synonyms.n: properties.description on models and columns, plus Markdown rules and glossary files under knowledge/ that agents retrieve.

verifiedQueries.n: NL-to-SQL pairs are Markdown files under knowledge/sql/. The wren memory store command writes them.

nl2sql.n: Agents generate governed SQL through wren query and wren ask. Wren AI Cloud adds a GenBI UI.

ontology.n: No ontology layer in the MDL reference. Models, relationships, views, and cubes are the objects.

graph.n: No graph query language in the MDL reference or CLI.

vector.n: A local LanceDB memory index gives hybrid retrieval over schema and stored pairs. Needs the memory extra.

mcp.n: wren serve mcp exposes query, dry-run, schema, and knowledge tools over stdio or HTTP. Needs the mcp extra.

governance.n: Row and column security is in Wren AI Cloud and Enterprise Plus, not open source. OSS can omit model columns.

openStandard.n: Engine, SDK, and skills are Apache 2.0. Reads and writes Apache Ossie 0.1.1 and the 0.2.0.dev0 draft.

offers: MDL models, relationships, views, and cubes kept as YAML in Git.
NL-to-SQL pairs and business rules stored under knowledge/ and recalled by agents.
Local MCP server with query, dry-run, schema, and knowledge tools.
Imports from dbt, OpenMetadata, and Apache Ossie, and exports to Ossie.
Connects to the data sources in the connect guide on one Apache DataFusion engine.
gaps: Row and column security, the GenBI UI, and dashboards are commercial (Wren AI Cloud or Enterprise Plus).
Traversing a relationship handle directly in a query is not supported yet (issue 2688).
The golden NL-SQL eval runner is listed as in development.
The connect guide lists fewer data sources than the README figure of 22+.
No ontology or graph feature.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Install the CLI with pip install wrenai, generate or import an MDL project, and add rules and NL-to-SQL pairs under knowledge/. Connect your agent through wren serve mcp or the Wren skills, and query with wren query.

snippet.title: MDL model on a physical table
snippet.code:
name: customers
table_reference:
  catalog: jaffle_shop
  schema: main
  table: customers
primary_key: customer_id
columns:
  - name: customer_id
    type: INTEGER
    is_primary_key: true
    not_null: true
  - name: first_name
    type: VARCHAR

vendors.name: Malloy (with Publisher)
vendors.tagline: Open-source semantic modeling and query language; Publisher serves models with an MCP endpoint.
vendors.verdictNote: Malloy models define sources, joins, and measures in code, and Publisher serves them to agents through an MCP endpoint.

artifacts.name: Malloy semantic models (sources, joins, dimensions, measures, views)
Malloy Publisher (server, REST API, web UI)

metrics.n: Measures are declared on sources with aggregate expressions and saved with the model.

dimensions.n: Dimensions and views are declared on sources. Views are saved queries that agents can reuse.

relationships.n: join_one, join_many, and join_cross declare joins on a source. Primary keys enable the with shortcut.

synonyms.n: Annotations on fields and sources carry descriptions that agents read through Publisher. No synonyms field found.

verifiedQueries.n: No question-to-query store. Named views and queries are returned by malloy_getContext to guide agents.

nl2sql.n: No first-party NL-to-query generation. malloy_getContext retrieves relevant fields for a question, and the agent writes the Malloy.

ontology.n: No ontology layer found in the language reference or Publisher docs.

graph.n: No graph query language. Joins are modeled as a data graph for correct aggregation, but queries are not graph queries.

vector.n: No vector search found in the Malloy or Publisher docs.

mcp.n: Publisher serves MCP at localhost:4040/mcp with discovery, query, compile, reload, and docs search tools.

governance.n: Givens, #(authorize), and #(access_filter) gate sources and rows. Givens are behind an experimental flag. Publisher has no built-in authentication.

openStandard.n: Malloy is MIT-licensed open source. No Apache Ossie import or export found in the docs.

offers: Models in code with sources, joins, dimensions, and measures, compiled to each database dialect.
Publisher serves models over REST, a web UI, and MCP.
malloy_getContext finds relevant sources, views, and fields for a plain-English question.
malloy_compile checks agent-written Malloy and returns diagnostics without running a query.
Supports DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, Postgres, MySQL, Trino, and Presto.
gaps: No first-party NL-to-SQL, verified-query store, or synonyms field. The agent writes Malloy.
Publisher has no built-in authentication and its MCP port is open. Put a gateway in front.
Row-level access relies on givens, which sit behind an experimental flag.
No Apache Ossie import or export found.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Write Malloy models for your core sources, run Publisher, and point your agent at its MCP endpoint. Add annotations and named views so the agent finds the right fields, and test that your LLM writes valid Malloy.

snippet.title: Malloy sources with a primary key, a measure, and a join

vendors.name: Honeydew
vendors.tagline: Semantic layer defined in YAML, with an AI analyst, APIs, and an MCP server.
vendors.verdictNote: Entities, attributes, metrics, and relations are first-party objects, with Deep Analysis, an MCP server, row-level security, and Apache Ossie import and export.

artifacts.name: Context layer (instructions, skills, external knowledge, memory)
Snowflake Native App (semantic query and model update API)
Apache Ossie converter (import and export, tracks draft spec)

metrics.n: Metrics are aggregations defined once at an entity granularity and recomputed for any slice or join.

dimensions.n: Source and calculated attributes on entities. Domains choose which fields are exposed.

relationships.n: Entities declare relations with rel_type and key fields. Honeydew finds the join path from them.

synonyms.n: AI metadata on domains, entities, attributes, and metrics holds descriptions, synonyms, and allowed values.

verifiedQueries.n: No verified question-to-SQL store in the docs. Agents take sample questions for routing, and context items hold instructions and skills.

nl2sql.n: Deep Analysis runs multi-step analysis. The semantic compiler writes the SQL, not the LLM. Also reachable from Slack, Teams, MCP.

ontology.n: No ontology layer found. Entities, relations, and domains are the modeling objects.

graph.n: No graph query language found. GraphQL API exposes the platform, not graph queries.

vector.n: No vector search found in the docs.

mcp.n: MCP server at mcp.honeydew.cloud with OAuth. Tools cover analysis, model browsing, warehouse discovery, and model editing.

governance.n: Row-level security via domain filters or warehouse policies, user access control, Git change approval, and CI/CD.

openStandard.n: Bidirectional Apache Ossie converter kept in the Ossie repository. It tracks a draft spec that may change.

offers: Metrics defined once per entity, with join paths resolved from declared relations.
AI metadata holds descriptions, synonyms, and allowed values on entities, attributes, and metrics.
Deep Analysis and agents answer questions, with SQL compiled by the semantic compiler.
MCP server works with Claude, Cursor, Snowflake Intelligence, and other clients.
Row-level security, user access control, and Git workflows for model changes.
Import and export with Apache Ossie.
gaps: Snowflake is the GA platform. Databricks and BigQuery support are Beta and need support to enable.
No stored question-to-SQL pairs. Sample questions only route questions to agents.
The Apache Ossie spec is an early draft, so the converter may change.
No ontology, graph, or vector feature found in the docs.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Define entities, relations, and metrics in a Honeydew workspace, expose a domain to an agent, and add AI metadata with synonyms. Use Deep Analysis, or connect your own agent or Snowflake Cortex Agents through the MCP server.

snippet.title: A metric defined on an entity
snippet.code:
type: metric
entity: lineitem
name: revenue
description: revenue, as defined in TPC-H Q3, Q5 and others
datatype: number
sql: |-
  sum(lineitem.l_extendedprice * (1 - lineitem.l_discount))

notes.text: Vendor-run by dbt Labs, blog dated 7 Apr 2026. Dataset: ACME Insurance (from data.world), 11 questions run 20 times each. On the original schema (all 11 questions), text-to-SQL scored 64.5% and the Semantic Layer 72.7% with both Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.3 Codex. After 3 dbt models were added, the Semantic Layer scored 98.2% (Sonnet 4.6) and 100.0% (GPT-5.3 Codex), and text-to-SQL scored 90.0% and 84.1%. Bodo (Sep 2026) reported 220 of 220 correct with its own PyDough pipeline on a local SQLite replica, which is not the dbt setup.

sources.t: Semantic Layer vs. Text-to-SQL: 2026 Benchmark Update (dbt)
dbt Discourse thread on the benchmark

notes.text: Vendor-run by Cube staff, blog and arXiv paper dated 28 Apr 2026. Dataset: Cleaned Contoso Retail in ClickHouse, 100 questions, single-shot. Adding a 4 KB hand-written markdown semantic document to the schema raised accuracy: Opus 4.7 50.5% to 67.7%, Sonnet 4.6 46.5% to 68.7%, GPT-5.4 45.5% to 68.7%. The semantic layer in this test was the markdown file, not a running Cube deployment.

sources.t: Cube blog: paired benchmark across three frontier models

notes.text: Vendor-run by AtScale, white paper blog dated 8 Aug 2024. Dataset: TPC-DS, 40 questions, with 3 retries allowed on SQL syntax errors. A control given only table schemas and primary and foreign keys scored 20%, and the AtScale semantic layer with its query engine scored 92.5%. The blog does not name the LLM. AtScale launched a public text-to-SQL leaderboard on 6 Nov 2024.

sources.t: AtScale: natural language prompting with semantic layer and GenAI

notes.topic: Apache Ossie status for these vendors
notes.text: OSI is renamed Apache Ossie (incubating). dbt v1.12 reads Ossie JSON documents, Wren and Honeydew document import and export, and Cube documents conversion as Preview (changelog 16 Oct 2026). AtScale joined OSI on 27 Jan 2026. No Ossie support was found in the Malloy docs.

sources.t: dbt: Apache Ossie semantic layer documents

notes.text: Cube hosts a remote MCP server at cubecloud.dev/mcp with OAuth. The earlier local npm package is deprecated in favor of it, per its README.
Honeydew docs mark Snowflake as the supported platform and label Databricks and Google BigQuery support as Beta, available through support.
Current Wren docs define MDL as YAML files that compile to target/mdl.json. Older material shows MDL as JSON.
